children: continued its campaign to have plaintiffs in a lawsuit seeking to block its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery
post a $1.88B surety bond to cover the company’s losses, including ticking fees, if it ultimately prevails.
Under the terms of the merger agreement, Paramount
shareholders $650M per quarter beginning October 1. Because the trial is set for March 2027, Paramount
would be required to pay $1.3B in ticking fees plus another $190M in incremental financing costs and legal fees.
In a brief filed on Tuesday, Paramount
said the plaintiffs are obligated to post a preliminary injunction bond under antitrust laws and the Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

“Paramount simply asks that Plaintiffs honor what the Clayton Act requires: a bond that will compensate Paramount for the damage it will suffer if the injunction proves improvidently granted, i.e., if Paramount ultimately prevails in the litigation and was therefore wrongly prevented from consummating the merger now, as it is prepared to do,” the filing states.
The plaintiffs, however, which include twelve state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America, argue that Paramount
is ineligible for a bond since it was Paramount that agreed to halt the merger.
